page: Amazon Web Services r7g.2xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by custom 64-bit ARM architecture. It features 8 dedicated physical cores utilizing the AWS Graviton3 processor family with Neoverse-V1 cores clocked at 2.6 GHz. The CPU allocation provides one thread per core with no hyperthreading. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The instance operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results indicate strong memory performance, with a PassMark memory score in the top 25% and a read-only small-block memory bandwidth of 774.63 GB/sec. Large-block read and write bandwidths reach 184.3 GB/sec and 68.94 GB/sec respectively. CPU performance is moderate, with a PassMark CPU score of 6073.06, placing it in the bottom 25%. Multi-core stress-ng performance reaches 12242.92, while single-core performance sits at 1533.19. Cryptographic operations are supported via hardware AES acceleration, though the ARM architecture lacks x86-specific vector extensions like AVX.

Given its high memory density and strong memory bandwidth, the r7g.2xlarge is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or high-performance x86 vector instructions. It is well-suited for database operations, caching layers like Redis (achieving 13.53 million SET operations per second in testing), static web serving, and memory-intensive data processing. However, it exhibits lower performance in text generation for large language models, making it less optimal for heavy AI inference tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services r7g.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 8 dedicated physical ARM64 cores powered by AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processors running at 2.6 GHz. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, it delivers 64.0 GB of system memory, establishing a high 8.0 GB per core ratio. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on a 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Performance testing highlights a strong memory subsystem, with a PassMark memory score in the top 25% and a small-block read bandwidth of 774.63 GB/sec, though overall CPU compute benchmarks lean average to weak. This hardware profile makes the r7g.2xlarge highly suitable for memory-intensive applications, such as Redis caching, database operations, and static web serving, where high memory capacity and bandwidth are prioritized over raw floating-point compute power.
